newsitem.title: CANADA: Hollinger International says Telegraph upping price.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger International says Telegraph upping price.

text.p: Press baron Conrad Black's Hollinger International Inc. officially ended the latest skirmish in the British broadsheet newspaper price war on Thursday, hiking its Daily Telegraph newspaper cover price starting next week.
This matches a recent rise by Rupert Murdoch's The Times.

The Telegraph will mirror The Times' five pence (8 cents) a copy price rise from Tuesday to Friday, and will bump up the Saturday price five pence vs. a 10 pence (16 cents) rise in the Saturday Times.
Like its arch rival, The Telegraph will also cancel a voucher system for the Tuesday paper that allowed participating readers to purchase it for 10 pence.
Hollinger said the increases will pull circulation revenues back nearly to the levels which preceded the price war between the two London-based broadsheet newspapers.
The latest moves would add almost $20 million to The Telegraph's annualized pre-tax profit.

"And, along with substantial year-over-year advertising revenue increases, (the price increases) will raise The Telegraph's operating profit levels to the highest point in the company's history," Hollinger said.
Beginning in the fourth quarter, current circulation and operating margins at The Daily and Sunday Telegraphs will be well above previous projections, Hollinger said.

"The Daily Telegraph emerges from this period of almost unprecedented intense competition with a steadily rising circulation, and a younger and more prosperous readership than at any time since reliable data was available," said Hollinger Chairman Conrad Black in a statement.
"These developments should make even higher levels of profitability achievable," he added.
Black said The Telegraph's circulation has risen to its highest point in recent years.
Hollinger Inc. owns 57.8 percent of Hollinger International which in turn owns The Telegraph.
